newsitem.title: JAPAN: GDP data confirm Japan's economic recovery -- EPA.
newsitem.headline: GDP data confirm Japan's economic recovery -- EPA.

text.p: Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) figures for the July-September period confirm that the nation's economy is on a gradual recovery track, Economic Planning Agency Vice Minister Shimpei Nukaya told a news conference on Tuesday.
"We have confirmed that the gradual recovery is continuing. This will become clearer in the October-December period," Nukaya said.
"It is possible for us to achieve the government forecast of about 2.5 percent growth (in GDP) this fiscal year."
The EPA explained that Japan would need 0.63 percent GDP growth in each of the last two quarters of the fiscal year to achieve the 2.5 percent target for the year.
Nukaya also said Japan's economic recovery was moving towards self-sustainability led by private demand.
Public investment fell in the July-September quarter while private corporate investment rose, he said.

Asked about the need to come up with a supplementary budget with additional public works spending, Nukaya said: "There is no need for a type of supplementary budget which will add additional public spending."
But he added that the government may consider moving forward to this fiscal year some public works projects to be budgeted in next year's fiscal budget.

Nukaya said there were no worries that the economic recovery will slow down at the moment, but he added there was the possibility that growth may slow in the April-June period because of a planned rise in the consumption tax on April 1.
Nukaya said he wanted the Bank of Japan to continue its current easy monetary policy, which the BOJ governor has said places emphasis on putting the recovery on a firm track.
Nukaya said that private consumption was down slightly in the quarter due to the effects of a food poisoning epidemic this summer, but was now recovering.
Housing investment was down slightly due to a time lag between when construction was ordered and when it started, he said, adding housing investment was still strong.
Inventory adjustment was in its last stages and was unlikely to hinder growth in the next two quarters, he said.

Nukaya said it would be in line with the government policy to restructure state finances if special income tax cuts were ended. But the government had to keep in mind the economy's growth prospects for next fiscal year and consumer sentiment before making a final decision on the income tax cuts, he said.
